issues.t: Sudden loss of power from overheating battery contactors (recall)
issues.sym: The car shows a stop-safely or reduced-power warning and may lose drive power while moving, or it may refuse to go into Ready after being parked.
issues.why: The main contactors (heavy-duty switches that connect the high-voltage battery to the motors) can overheat and weld or fail, mostly on cars that see lots of DC fast charging and hard acceleration. Ford first used a software update to watch contactor heat, then moved to replacing the battery junction box on extended-range cars. Some cars repaired under the first recall were not fixed correctly and were recalled again.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls (22V-412, 23V-687, 25V-130 and 25V-441). If the warning appears while driving, pull over safely. The junction box replacement is free at a Ford EV dealer.

issues.t: Rear differential pinion shaft may break (recall)
issues.sym: Loss of drive power, or the car rolling when parked if the parking brake was not set. There may be no warning before it happens.
issues.why: The pinion shaft inside the rear drive unit's differential can fracture. With it broken, the rear motor can no longer drive or hold the wheels.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 26V-417 (Ford 26S50). Until it is repaired, always set the parking brake when you park. Dealers will repair or replace the rear differential free.

issues.t: Doors may not open from inside with a weak 12-volt battery (recall)
issues.sym: With a low 12-volt battery the electronic door buttons stop working, and the doors can stay locked after they close. Someone inside may not be able to get out with the normal buttons.
issues.why: The Mach-E uses electronic door latches that need 12-volt power. If the small battery drops very low, the latches may not release normally. Ford's software update changes how the latches behave at low voltage.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 25V-404 (Ford 25S65) and get the free software update. Learn where the manual interior door releases are and show your passengers.

issues.t: Park may not lock when selected (recall)
issues.sym: You shift to Park but the car is not actually held in Park and may roll away, especially on a slope.
issues.why: Software in the integrated park module may fail to lock the park mechanism when the driver selects Park. Ford fixes it with a software update.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 25V-863 (Ford 25C69). Accept the over-the-air update or have a dealer install it, and use the parking brake until then.

issues.t: Park rod may not engage (recall)
issues.sym: The car may roll after being put in Park.
issues.why: A defective park rod in the drive unit on a small number of 2025 cars may not engage the park lock.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 25V-394 (Ford 25C25). Dealers replace the park rod assembly free. Set the parking brake every time until it is done.

issues.t: Headlights and turn signals may stop working (recall)
issues.sym: Headlights, daytime running lights or turn signals go out, sometimes all at once, often with a lighting warning on the dash.
issues.why: Two separate faults: a lighting control module that can fail on 2025–2026 cars (fixed by software), and a burnt diode in the LED driver modules on some 2025 cars (fixed by replacing the modules).
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 25V-885 (Ford 25C71) and 25V-519 (Ford 25C39). Avoid night driving if the lights are out and book the free repair.

issues.t: Rearview camera freezes or goes blank (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into Reverse, the backup camera picture is delayed, frozen or black.
issues.why: A software error in the camera and display system, shared with many Ford and Lincoln models.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 25V-315. The fix is a free software update by over-the-air or at a dealer. Use your mirrors and look behind you until then.

issues.t: Rear seat belt buckles may not be anchored (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you notice. A buckle may feel loose or move more than it should.
issues.why: On some early cars the rear seat belt buckles were not attached properly, so they may not hold in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 21V-979. Dealers repair the buckle attachments free.

issues.t: Windshield may not be bonded properly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you notice; in a crash the windshield may come loose.
issues.why: The adhesive primer used on the windshield was not applied correctly at the factory on some early 2021 cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 21V-711. Dealers remove and reinstall the windshield free.

issues.t: Glass roof may not be bonded properly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you notice. Rarely, wind noise or movement from the fixed glass roof.
issues.why: The fixed panoramic glass roof on some early 2021 cars was not bonded properly and could detach while driving.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 21V-712. Dealers add adhesive to secure the roof free.

issues.t: Loose front subframe bolts (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end, or vague handling. Many owners noticed nothing.
issues.why: The bolts that hold the front subframe to the body may not have been tightened properly on some early cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 21V-140. Dealers inspect and tighten the bolts free.

issues.t: Right rear half shaft may break (recall)
issues.sym: A loud bang or clunk from the rear, then loss of drive to the rear wheels, or the car rolling in Park without the parking brake set.
issues.why: The right rear axle half shaft on some 2022 cars can break under load.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 22V-646. Dealers inspect and replace the half shaft free.

issues.t: Unexpected acceleration or loss of drive power from software (recall)
issues.sym: The car may speed up, slow down or lose drive power without warning.
issues.why: Powertrain control software on some early all-wheel-drive cars might not detect an internal error, which could cause unintended acceleration, deceleration or loss of power.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 22V-333. The fix is a free software update at a dealer or over the air.

issues.t: Loss of brake assist and ABS after software update (recall)
issues.sym: Brake, ABS and stability warnings come on, the pedal feels hard, and driver-assist features stop working.
issues.why: A faulty over-the-air update to the anti-lock brake module on a small number of 2021 cars could disable power brake assist, ABS and stability control. A few cars were later fixed incorrectly and recalled again.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 24V-777 and 25V-513. If the warnings appear, drive carefully to a dealer or have it towed; the fix is a free calibration update.

issues.t: Rear quarter window trim may come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise or a loose-looking trim piece at the small rear side window. In bad cases the trim can fall off while driving.
issues.why: The trim on the rear side quarter window glass may not be fastened securely.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 26V-487 (Ford 26S56). Dealers inspect and replace the glass assemblies free as needed.

issues.t: Windshield wipers may stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The front wipers stop or work only some of the time, which makes driving in rain or snow dangerous.
issues.why: The front wiper motor can fail on some 2023–2024 cars. The same recall covers some Maverick and Bronco Sport models.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 24V-594. Dealers inspect and replace the wiper motor free.

issues.t: Wrong charge reading after battery module replacement (recall)
issues.sym: The charge level or range shown may not match the real battery charge, so the car can lose power sooner than expected.
issues.why: Cars that had their battery energy control module replaced may have the wrong software. It can misreport the state of charge and raise fire risk after repeated DC fast charging. It affects a small number of cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 26V-582 (Ford 26S68). Avoid repeated fast charging until the free software update is done.

issues.t: 12-volt battery drains overnight while plugged in
issues.sym: After charging overnight the car seems completely dead: no unlock, dark screens and the FordPass app showing deep sleep.
issues.why: On early cars built through February 3, 2021, the car's software stopped topping up the small 12-volt battery while the car was plugged in. The 12-volt battery then ran flat. Cold weather made it more likely.
issues.next: Jump the 12-volt system from the posts behind the front bumper access panel if needed. Ask a Ford EV dealer to confirm the module reprogramming from the 2021 bulletin and later updates are done.

issues.t: 12-volt battery failure leaves car dead
issues.sym: The car won't unlock or turn on, screens stay dark, charging won't start, or random warnings appear.
issues.why: Like gas cars, the Mach-E has a small 12-volt battery that runs locks, screens and computers. When it weakens with age or is drained, the car can't wake up even if the big battery is full. Many owners replace it around the 3-year mark.
issues.next: Have the 12-volt battery tested. Replace it with the correct AGM type and have the battery monitor reset. Keep software and 12-volt related recalls up to date.

issues.t: Clunk from rear when accelerating or braking
issues.sym: A clunk or knock from the back of the car when you speed up or brake, going forward or in reverse.
issues.why: On cars built through October 5, 2021, a bushing in the rear upper trailing arm can make metal-to-metal contact under heavy load. Ford bulletin 22-2253 covers it.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about TSB 22-2253. The fix is replacing one or both rear upper trailing arms.

issues.t: Front motor whine at 30-40 mph
issues.sym: A whine from the front of the car at steady speeds around 30 to 40 mph, with no warning lights.
issues.why: Ford traced it to software settings in the front drive unit on all-wheel-drive cars. Some whine is normal for this motor design.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about TSB 23-2168 (later 23-2261), which updates the powertrain software. No parts are replaced.

issues.t: Water leaking into the liftgate
issues.sym: After rain or a car wash, water drips from the liftgate latch, handle or close button.
issues.why: Water gets past the seals around the tail lamps mounted in the liftgate. Bulletin 23-2360 covers cars built through September 29, 2023.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about TSB 23-2360. The fix is resealing both liftgate tail lamps with butyl tape.

issues.t: Wind noise from mirrors and front pillars
issues.sym: A whistle or rush of wind near the side mirrors or windshield pillars, mostly around 25 to 40 mph.
issues.why: The foam seals under the mirrors and around the front door glass don't seal well. Ford bulletin 24-2230 covers cars built through July 9, 2024.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about TSB 24-2230 (replaced 24-2002). The fix is refitting the mirror seals and replacing foam pieces.

issues.t: BlueCruise steering is jittery or misses stopped cars
issues.sym: With BlueCruise hands-free driving on, the steering wobbles or jerks in the lane. In rare cases the system did not react to stopped vehicles ahead.
issues.why: BlueCruise relies on cameras, radar and software. NHTSA opened an investigation (EA25001) after crashes in which BlueCruise-equipped Mach-Es hit stopped vehicles.
issues.next: Keep your eyes on the road and be ready to steer and brake at all times. Install software updates and check for any recall that comes from the investigation.
